title: `get_real_name()` returns a middle part of names with more than two dotted parts
spec:
This is the sqlparse library (Python 3, no dependencies). Run the tests with `PYTHONPATH=. python3 -m pytest -q -p no:cacheprovider tests`.

For a fully qualified name with three or more parts, `get_real_name()` returns the second part instead of the object name.

```python
import sqlparse
ident = sqlparse.parse('db.schema.tbl.col')[0].tokens[0]
ident.get_real_name(), ident.get_name(), ident.get_parent_name()
```
Expected: `('col', 'col', 'db')`
Actual: `('schema', 'schema', 'db')`

Aliased and function names are affected the same way: for `x.y.z AS w` the real name should be `'z'` (actual `'y'`, alias `'w'` is correct), and for `mydb.sch.func(1)` it should be `'func'` (actual `'sch'`).

The real name is the part after the last dot. Two-part names such as `a.b` (real name `'b'`) already work and must keep working, and `get_parent_name()` should keep returning the first part.
acceptance: `get_real_name()` and `get_name()` return the last dotted part for names of any length, including aliased names and function calls
Regression tests are added and the full test suite passes
